title: mouse without borders don't let me connect after blackout

actions.label: Validate key generation and signed peer pairing

setup: Keep the reported post-blackout scenario and preserve existing settings; do not mix executable versions or bypass trust checks.
prerequisites: Two isolated Windows PCs on the same private network, same supported version/install scope and trusted product components.
steps: 1. Reproduce new-key generation and existing-peer reconnection separately on the reported release; correlate the failure with the IPC rejection reason.
2. Repeat both operations using a supported signed build containing the correction, including independently signed different-leaf components.
3. Pair in both directions and reboot/reconnect once; classify any remaining network or identity failures separately.
reproduce.expected_result: Settings key generation and valid peer pairing work without signer-equality rejection; altered/untrusted components remain rejected and unrelated connection failures are not declared fixed.
reproduce.version_requirement: Reported0.102.3001 and a supported signed build containing PR51789
reproduce.title: Separate Settings signer rejection from network recovery

judgment.rationale: The previously inspected archive establishes the signer-rejection class. The new Settings/key symptoms reinforce that route, but do not prove the blackout is causal or every connection failure shares it. Preserve the report under50795 and its open signer fix rather than request the same ZIP again or recommend mixed-release executable replacement.
judgment.recommended_action: Consolidate the new key-generation/reconnection evidence with50795 and validate the open signer fix using supported signed product components.
evidence: PowerToys0.102.3001 from Microsoft Store; the title reports MWB will not connect after a blackout, but the body provides no explicit failing action or error banner.
The supplied diagnostic ZIP was inspected privately: seven relevant Settings/MWB text entries contain repeated untrusted-signature rejection.
Primary50795 remains open and covers the Settings-to-MWB peer-verification rejection class. A released repair is not established.
The October31 follow-up reports both new-key generation and existing-peer connection fail after updating to0.102.3001, even when elevated, and supplies a screenshot.

Open PR51789 replaces equal leaf-certificate bytes with independent trusted Microsoft-signature checks while preserving peer identity gates. Its exact affected project and50 selected IPC tests were independently executed successfully during the earlier scheduled update.

fix_assessment.rationale: Primary50795 and open PR51789 cover the diagnostic-confirmed signer rejection. This is not a merged/shipped fix or proof that all transport failures are resolved.
